Before I put on any makeup, I mix one pump Cetaphil moisturizer with SPF 30 with 2 pumps Aveeno BB Cream from fair to light, which also has SPF30. I love the color that I get with the Aveeno, but by itself, the color is too dark for me. Mixing it with the Cetaphil makes the color more sheer, which makes my skin look super glow-y (even my mom says so!).

 

For reference, here's the Ingredients for Cetaphil:

Active Ingredients

Avobenzone 3%, Octisalate 5%, Octocrylene 7%

Inactive Ingredients

Water, Isopropyl Lauroyl Sarcosinate, Glycerin, Dimethicone, Diisopropyl Sebacate, Silica, Polymethyl Methacrylate, Aluminum Starch Octenylsuccinate, Sucrose Tristearate, Dimethiconol, Pentylene Glycol, Polysorbate 61, Sodium Stearoyl Glutamate, Phenoxyethanol, Caprylyl Glycol, Tocopheryl Acetate, Glycyrrhetinic Acid, Panthenol, Triethanolamine, Allantoin, Carbomer, Potassium Sorbate, Zinc Gluconate, Xanthan Gum, Disodium EDTA, Hydroxypalmitoyl Sphinganine.

 

Ingredients for Aveeno:

Active Ingredients

Homosalate (5%) (Sunscreen), Octinoxate (7.5%) (Sunscreen), Octisalate (5%) (Sunscreen), Oxybenzone (2%) (Sunscreen)

Inactive Ingredients

Water, PPG-3 Myristyl Ether Neoheptanoate, Phenyl Trimethicone, Glycine Soja (Soybean) Seed Extract, Butylene Glycol, Hydrogenated Palm Kernel Glycerides, Silica, PEG-100 Stearate, Glyceryl Stearate, Cetearyl Alcohol, Glycerin, Hydroxyethyl Acrylate/Sodium Acryloyldimethyl Taurate Copolymer, Caprylyl Glycol, Isohexadecane, Bisabolol, Triethoxycaprylylsilane, Fragrance, Citric Acid, Magnesium Aluminum Silicate, Cetearyl Glucoside, Polysorbate 20, p-Anisic Acid, Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate, Hydrogenated Palm Glycerides, Urea, Sodium PCA, Cetyl Hydroxyethylcellulose, Polysorbate 60, Xanthan Gum, Tetrasodium EDTA, Hexylene Glycol, Trehalose, Polyquaternium-51, Triacetin, Methylisothiazolinone, Sodium Hyaluronate, Titanium Dioxide, Mica, Iron Oxides

 

I know mixing sunscreen with other products is generally bad because it makes the sunscreen less (or in-)effective. But are mixing these two specific chemical sunscreens a bad idea?

The only reason why people say its less effective is because your not applying the amount you need for good sun protection. Mixing two sunscreens together should not be bad. The only thing that is bad is when the sunscreens don't blend well and start rubbing off while you try to apply it due to Inactive ingredients not getting along.

Both water based, the Cetaphil is a good spf, although I personally wouldn't recommend an spf with oxybenzone in it: the Aveeno bb cream. Check out ewg.org if you'd like information on the hazards of certain skincare products. In regards to mixing, no reason to worry whatsoever. I do a layer of spf 15 primer, and then a sunscreen. Ontop of my usual toning and moisturizing. If you were mixing sunscreen with an ordinary moisturizer, it would for sure be diluted. But some places sell spf boosters to add to moisturizers which is a nice alternative :)

I wouldn't mix sunscreens, especially because some ingredients are pretty unstable (looking at you Avobenzone). Usually other ingredients have to be added to the sunscreen to help stabilize the unstable ingredients. By mixing sunscreens you could be messing up this balanced mix and making some of the active UV blocking ingredients essentially useless.

A couple weekends ago I finally got to break in my new Weber Smokey Mountain 22" Smoker. I decided to start with ribs for shorter cook in order to dial in the temperature control.

Rib Prep

I have had good results with the preps steps on amazingribs.com. Two hours prior to smoking I started with a dry brine of the ribs. 10 - 15 minutes before the smoke, rubs were added to the two racks. My friend recently brought me back a couple of rubs from Kansas City, Jack Stack and the Squeal. I figured this would be a good opportunity for a side by side comparison.

Smoke Prep

On my Weber kettle, I typically use the snake method using a 2x2 snake. I was going to use 3x2x1 for the bigger WSM, but I heard they tend to run hot, so I setup 2x2x1. I fired up 20 coals in my chimney to start the snake. For wood I started with a bigger chunk of hickory, then a medium chunk of apple and followed up with another smaller chunk of hickory. I started with all three bottom vents fully open, and the water pan full.

Cooking

The ribs went on the smoker around 215 degrees, for cooking with the 3-2-1 method. Initially one rack was set a bit too close to the temperature probe, so this was reading low for a bit of the cook. Since I have the dual probe I decided to use one on each rack. Someone asked a couple weeks ago if there is a temperature difference between the top and bottom racks (this was originally intended to be posted on that other website). There is, the top runs 10-15 degrees warmer than the bottom. Surprisingly, the dial thermometer mounted to the dome was within a few degrees of my digital thermometer!

After two hours I mopped the ribs with apple juice. The temperature was maintaining right at 225 degrees with all three vents 100% open. At three hours I wrapped the ribs in heavy duty foil with apple juice for the Texas Crutch. At this time I also noticed the temp was dipping back down to around 210. I decided to check my snake, and found that it was already burning at the end. I added more charcoal on top of the coals that were still burning. A half an hour later I was hitting 250 degrees, still with all three vents wide open. Since the temp was on the rise, I closed all three to about 50%. For the next hour and a half it held steady around 230.

Five hours in I unwrapped the ribs, mopped with apple juice, and put them back on the smoker for the last hour. The temp was dropping again so I added a bit more charcoal to get me to the end. I held steady at around 225 for the remainder of the cook. To check doneness, I used the toothpick test to feel if the meat was tender. I find that this is easier for me to determine if the ribs are done than the bend test. At 5 hours and 45 minutes I pulled the ribs off the smoker.

Results

These were the best ribs I have ever cooked, better than even my favorite BBQ joint's ribs. Both rubs were fantastic, but I'll give the edge to the Squeal. My wife took a bite at the counter and then had to be dragged away to finish eating sitting down. I had barbeque sauce ready, but they were so juicy we both completely forgot about it. The smoke was perfect!

Next Time

The only criticism on the taste of the ribs was that they were slightly salty. This is due to the dry brine and the rubs containing salt. Usually if I make my own rubs, I leave out the salt in leau of the dry brine. As for the fire, I need my coals to last longer. Next time I will try at 3x3 snake, and start the fire with 30 coals. Hopefully this will allow me to close the vents a bit, and slow the burn of the snake down to last longer.
